Gojo/Ornament studies/Bourgoin constructions
Source study · Jules Bourgoin · 1883 scan

One construction, a coherent field

Geometric ornament recipes built from shared unmeasured reaches, ordered path words, finite phase cycles and explicit landmark seams. Every preview executes an imported native packet. The renderer supplies only a screen interpretation.

These are structural reconstructions and adaptations of selected diagrams in Théorie de l’ornement. Compare the source excerpt beside each field. Faithfulness, simplifications and open metric assumptions are stated individually.

A common plan is useful; one connected ink component is optional. Bourgoin distinguishes detached, contiguous, crossed and articulated motifs. Guides and source descriptions often explain the composition better than the final outline alone.

All constructions on one page · Standalone labelled SVG

B02 · imported native field

Basket rectangles and square gaps

Authored recipe · description of the generating construction

One elongated rectangle is reused twice vertically and twice after a quarter-turn. Neighbouring rectangle centres are staggered, and explicit split side contacts leave small square interstices; no square motif is placed in those gaps.

Authored source assessment. Rebuilt from the actual Fig. 188 arrangement: central side-to-side contacts, alternating horizontal/vertical elongated rectangles, and square gaps. Shared-reach proportions are selected; the book's drawn stroke widths are outside the native skeleton.

B08 · imported native field

Intersecting diagonal ribbons

Authored recipe · description of the generating construction

Two straight paired-line systems cross on an oblique disposition. Alternating narrow/wide separations create large diamond areas, narrow four-sided ribbon compartments, and small crossing compartments. All intended contacts are explicit endpoint roles; dotted construction guides and curves are omitted.

Authored source assessment. A revised Fig. 203 ribbon skeleton replacing the cranked-wave reading. This preserves the paired diagonal disposition and its compartment hierarchy; slopes, narrow/wide proportions and the finite crop remain selected rather than traced from raster pixels. The source's steeper short junction transitions remain simplified to straight ribbon lines.

B12 · imported native field

Closed stepped-arm compartments

Authored recipe · description of the generating construction

Two closed stepped-arm compartment prototypes alternate diagonally. One has two same-side arms with hands bent together; the other has opposed arms whose hands turn toward the body. Actual mirrored images supply the next row. Every source corner is retained as a port correspondence, so the closed white chambers and their diagonal junctions determine the field rather than open spiral strokes.

Authored source assessment. Reconstructed from the closed negative compartments of Plate 9 fig. 10. The two sixteen-corner contours, their opposed row handedness and their interlocking disposition follow the source. Finite shared-reach proportions are selected from the trace; printed ink width and exact raster coordinates are not native promises.

B13 · imported native field

Interlocking serif-I compartments

Authored recipe · description of the generating construction
